text: The ultrasound findings of a cystic mass with biliary dilation strongly suggest a choledochal cyst, despite the normal CA 19-9. To confirm the anatomy and rule out malignancy, I need a more detailed view. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRCP: Confirms a fusiform dilation of the common bile duct consistent with a Type I choledochal cyst. No evidence of intraductal stones or filling defects suggestive of malignancy. Normal pancreatic duct.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRCP confirms a Type I choledochal cyst, which explains your jaundice and pruritus due to biliary obstruction. However, given your significant weight loss and smoking history, we must rule out a concurrent malignancy within the cyst, so I will request an endoscopic ultrasound for biopsy. REQUEST TEST: Endoscopic_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Endoscopic_Ultrasound: Anechoic cystic mass in the common bile duct with smooth walls. No solid components, mural nodules, or suspicious masses identified within the cyst. No evidence of pancreatic or periampullary malignancy. Fine-needle aspiration of the cyst fluid shows benign biliary epithelial cells with no malignant cells detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging and biopsy results strongly support a diagnosis of a symptomatic Type I choledochal cyst without evidence of malignancy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Choledochal cyst
